japanese.name: Toyota
japanese.description: World's largest automaker, pioneer of hybrid technology with Prius. Known for reliability, innovation, and the Toyota Production System.
japanese.fact: The Toyota Corolla is the best-selling car of all time with over 50 million sold.

japanese.name: Honda
japanese.description: Engineering excellence, known for VTEC technology, motorcycles, and the legendary NSX supercar. World's largest engine manufacturer.
japanese.fact: Honda is the world's largest motorcycle manufacturer and also builds aircraft, robots, and power equipment.

japanese.name: Nissan
japanese.description: Makers of the iconic GT-R, pioneers of electric vehicles with Leaf. Strong motorsport heritage and innovative design.
japanese.fact: The Nissan GT-R is nicknamed 'Godzilla' because it dominates supercars at a fraction of the price.

japanese.name: Mazda
japanese.description: Famous for rotary engines and the MX-5 Miata, the best-selling sports car of all time. Kodo design language.
japanese.fact: The Mazda MX-5 Miata is the best-selling two-seat convertible sports car in history, with over 1 million sold.

japanese.name: Subaru
japanese.description: Symmetrical AWD and boxer engines. Rally legend with Impreza WRX and off-road capability.
japanese.fact: Subaru uses boxer engines in all its cars, which have lower center of gravity for better handling.

japanese.name: Mitsubishi
japanese.description: Rally champions with Lancer Evolution, Pajero off-road heritage, and innovative SUVs.
japanese.fact: The Lancer Evolution was developed to compete in the World Rally Championship and became a legend.

japanese.name: Suzuki
japanese.description: Kei car specialists, off-road legends with Jimny, and motorcycle manufacturing.
japanese.fact: The Suzuki Jimny has remained virtually unchanged for over 50 years due to its legendary off-road capability.

japanese.name: Lexus
japanese.description: Toyota's luxury division, known for refinement, hybrid technology, and the LFA supercar.
japanese.fact: The Lexus LS 400 shocked the world in 1989 with its Mercedes-beating refinement at launch.

japanese.name: Acura
japanese.description: Honda's luxury brand, first Japanese luxury marque. Known for NSX and SH-AWD technology.
japanese.fact: Acura was the first Japanese luxury brand, launching two years before Lexus and Infiniti.

japanese.name: Infiniti
japanese.description: Nissan's luxury division, known for design, V6 performance, and Q50 sports sedan.
japanese.fact: The Infiniti Q45 was the first Japanese car with a V8 engine and active suspension.

german.name: BMW
german.description: Bayerische Motoren Werke, ultimate driving machines, inline-6 engines, and M performance division.
german.fact: BMW started as an aircraft engine manufacturer – the blue and white logo represents a spinning propeller.

german.name: Mercedes-Benz
german.description: Inventors of the automobile, pioneers in safety, luxury, and the iconic 300SL Gullwing.
german.fact: Mercedes-Benz invented the first automobile in 1886 and the first diesel car in 1936.

german.name: Audi
german.description: Quattro AWD pioneers, advanced technology, and motorsport success with rally and Le Mans.
german.fact: The four rings of the Audi logo represent four companies that merged: Audi, DKW, Horch, and Wanderer.

german.name: Volkswagen
german.description: People's car, Beetle legend, Golf pioneer, and now electric revolution with ID series.
german.fact: The Volkswagen Beetle was produced for 65 years (1938-2003) with over 21 million built.

german.name: Porsche
german.description: Iconic 911, engineering perfection, motorsport dominance, and now the Taycan electric.
german.fact: Over 70% of all Porsches ever built are still on the road today.

german.name: Opel
german.description: German manufacturer known for Kadett, Astra, and Manta. Now part of Stellantis.
german.fact: Opel started as a sewing machine manufacturer before building cars, and was Germany's largest automaker in the 1920s.

german.name: Maybach
german.description: Ultra-luxury brand, now part of Mercedes-Benz, known for chauffeur-driven excellence.
german.fact: The Maybach 62 was so luxurious that it had a panoramic roof and could be ordered with a champagne cooler.

german.name: Smart
german.description: City car specialist, known for compact size, efficiency, and urban mobility.
german.fact: The Smart Fortwo is so small that you can park it perpendicular to the curb in some European cities.

american.name: Ford
american.description: Assembly line revolution, Model T, Mustang, F-Series trucks, and American icon.
american.fact: The Ford F-150 has been America's best-selling vehicle for over 40 years.

american.name: Chevrolet
american.description: Heart of America, Corvette legend, Camaro muscle, and Silverado trucks.
american.fact: The Chevrolet small-block V8, introduced in 1955, is one of the most produced engines in history.

american.name: Dodge
american.description: Muscle car heritage, Challenger, Charger, Viper, and HEMI V8 power.
american.fact: The Dodge Viper was developed with no electronic aids – no ABS, no traction control, just raw power.

american.name: Cadillac
american.description: American luxury, fins, Eldorado, and modern performance with V series.
american.fact: Cadillac was the first car company to mass-produce V8 engines and electric starters.

american.name: Tesla
american.founder: Martin Eberhard, Marc Tarpenning, Elon Musk
american.description: Electric revolution, Autopilot, Model S, and sustainable energy focus.
american.fact: Tesla's Gigafactory in Nevada is the largest building in the world by footprint.

american.name: Jeep
american.description: Military heritage, Wrangler off-road legend, and 4x4 capability.
american.fact: The original Jeep Willys MB was designed in just 75 days and over 600,000 were built for WWII.

american.name: Lincoln
american.description: Presidential luxury, Continental icon, and American elegance.
american.fact: Lincoln has been the official state car of US presidents since 1939.

american.name: Buick
american.description: Premium American brand, Riviera design icon, and Chinese market leader.
american.fact: Buick is incredibly popular in China, where it's considered a luxury status symbol.
